Definition: from G737; fresh, i.e. (by implication) complete:--perfect.
BiblicalUsage: Perfect here means complete, fitted and furnished, and it is used once, for the man of God. All Scripture is given that the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for complete carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the promise, that Scripture does not leave the man of God half-furnished, but fits him out for every good work.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
